operations.specification: Create a new user account in the 'todo_users' table for the minimal Todo List application. This operation verifies that the email provided is not already registered (enforced by a unique constraint on the email field), validates password strength, and securely hashes the password before storing it in the 'password_hash' column. The operation also timestamps the creation using the 'created_at' field and associates this identity for isolated resource access. Upon successful registration, JWT tokens (access and refresh) are issued for authentication. The operation enforces all business rules defined in analysis, including email uniqueness, password policy (minimum 8 characters with letters and numbers), and ensures no other user data is accessible or disclosed. Only the fields present in the schema—'email' and 'password_hash'—are utilized for user credentials.
operations.description:
This endpoint creates a new user account leveraging the unique email constraint and secure password hashing mechanisms described in the 'todo_users' schema. Registration validates both the proper format and strength of the supplied email and password, conforming to the system's minimum password requirements.

All registration data is written directly to the 'todo_users' table, with explicit assignment of the current timestamp to 'created_at' and a properly hashed representation of the password in 'password_hash'. A new, unguessable UUID is generated for the account's 'id' primary key.

The registration process returns issued JWT tokens for session authentication, as mandated by requirements for immediate login after register. The only information returned is that which is strictly allowed by the schema and policy—principally, authentication token payloads and the user's identifier. No profile or extended metadata exists or is exposed here.

Strict privacy guarantees are enforced in every step. Cross-user access is impossible due to business logic and constraints in the schema. Error handling carefully avoids leaking information about other users or whether an email is already registered beyond the minimal allowed indication.

This operation is the single authorized entry point for user registration into the Todo List system. It can be used once per email. Every other authentication operation depends upon successful completion of this step for each user.
operations.summary: Register a new user in the 'todo_users' table with unique email and hashed password.

requestBody.description: Email and password data for new user registration. Password must meet minimal strength policy. Email must be unique among all user accounts.

responseBody.description: Authentication payload for successful registration, including JWT tokens and user identification info.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Authenticate a user by verifying the provided email and password against records in the 'todo_users' table, using the hashed password ('password_hash') for comparison. Upon successful authentication, a new access token and refresh token are created, and a session record is written in the 'todo_user_sessions' table capturing the user's 'id', session creation metadata, IP, referrer, and URL. This endpoint enables login by validated, registered users only, with strict privacy enforcement to block cross-user data access. All authentication logic strictly references fields and patterns guaranteed by the schemas.
operations.description:
This endpoint receives a user-provided email and password for authentication, referencing the unique email and password_hash fields of the 'todo_users' schema for validation. Email lookups are performed via the unique index on 'email', and password checking is done via hash comparison using the policy described in requirements documentation.

A successful match results in JWT access/refresh token issuance and a new entry in 'todo_user_sessions', which fully captures the session context via IP, referrer, URL, created_at, and references back to the authenticated user's id. This audit and tracking process is critical for secure session management and is required by security and privacy requirements.

This endpoint returns an authentication payload (tokens and user ID) and does not expose any data except as strictly necessary for session establishment. Errors for invalid credentials are handled generically, providing no clues about which credential was incorrect, and ensuring denial for disabled/nonexistent accounts.

Logout is performed by revoking the refresh token/session via a separate endpoint, not included here but implied by standard token flows. The session audit trail may be referenced for administrative or investigative purposes but is not user-accessible in this minimal system.

The login operation is only accessible to users who have registered via the '/auth/user/join' endpoint. No admin or third-party login is permitted in this application context.
operations.summary: Authenticate a user by email and password, create session and issue JWT access/refresh tokens from 'todo_users' and 'todo_user_sessions'.

requestBody.description: User login credentials—email and password. Used for authentication only.

responseBody.description: Authentication result including JWT payload and user/session identifiers.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Refresh an authenticated user's session by validating the provided refresh token and establishing a new session entry in 'todo_user_sessions'. This operation is available only to authenticated users with non-expired, non-revoked refresh tokens. It captures all session attributes (IP, referrer, URL) via the session schema and issues new tokens as required by the authentication policy. Underlying logic references only legitimate entries in the user and session tables, providing robust, auditable token flows in compliance with privacy and authentication requirements.
operations.description:
This endpoint receives a refresh token from an authenticated user and, after validation, issues a new set of authentication tokens and creates a new session record in 'todo_user_sessions'. The session record archives the session metadata for audit purposes, including the IP, referrer, and creation timestamp, referenced by the user's unique identifier.

Refresh tokens may only be used while valid and non-expired. The expiration and revocation policy is enforced by 'expired_at' in the 'todo_user_sessions' schema, with null indicating session is still active.

Fails if the token is invalid, expired, revoked, or does not map to a recognized session/user. No additional user or session data is revealed—only what is allowed by JWT policy. The refresh mechanism is fundamental to providing seamless, secure session lifecycle and minimizes login frequency for the user.

Upon successful refresh, the endpoint emits a signed JWT payload plus a refresh token with the proper expiration. Sessions are logged for compliance and audit.

The operation is not accessible publicly and strictly enforces session-based authentication policies as defined by requirements.
operations.summary: Refresh a user session by validating refresh token and issuing new tokens; update 'todo_user_sessions'.

requestBody.description: Payload containing the refresh token. Used only for token renewal.

responseBody.description: Renewed session authentication tokens and metadata for the logged-in user.

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: Allow an authenticated user to initiate a password reset process if they can demonstrate control of the registered email. The system sends a one-time, time-limited secure reset token to the email address in the 'todo_users' table, if it exists. Actual password resets happen through a follow-up operation that consumes this token. Operation references only the 'email' and relevant system policy; no state change occurs in the user table until the reset token is redeemed. Only valid, existing users may use this operation and error messages are never specific about whether an email address is present.
operations.description:
This operation initiates the password reset process for a user, conforming to the system's policy for secure account recovery. The endpoint receives an email address and, if it matches an entry in 'todo_users', sends a one-time password reset token to that address. The email field is validated for format and referenced via the unique constraint on 'todo_users.email'.

No information about account existence is disclosed in the response, and failure scenarios are handled generically. The password reset token is time-limited, typically valid for 15–30 minutes, and is stored only in a system-maintained context, never in the user table. Business logic for actual password reset is handled separately via token consumption. The operation is required for users who've lost their password or cannot access their account using normal credentials.

This endpoint is only accessible to non-authenticated users—those who need to recover access. Limits on request frequency should be applied to prevent abuse but are outside schema scope.

Related operations: password reset document redemption (not shown), login/join, session refresh. Security logging and rate limiting are implied.
operations.summary: Initiate password reset by issuing recovery token to email if found in 'todo_users'.

requestBody.description: Registered email for password reset initiation. No other fields.

responseBody.description: Confirmation of reset flow start (never indicates whether email exists).

operations.name: resetPassword

operations.specification: Redeem a valid, unexpired password reset token to change the user's password in the 'todo_users' table. This operation matches a token, performs validation (including password strength/policy), updates the 'password_hash' field on the matching user, resets the 'updated_at' timestamp, and invalidates the reset token (single-use principle). This ensures account security while allowing a user to regain control of their account via a secure email-based process. No other fields are changed, and audit logs are updated for compliance.
operations.description:
This endpoint performs the actual password reset, redeeming a one-time-use, time-limited reset token that was previously issued. The reset token is validated, and if valid, the new password provided is hashed following the same policy as registration. The 'password_hash' field in 'todo_users' is replaced, and the 'updated_at' timestamp is updated to indicate account change.

If the token is missing, expired, or already redeemed, the operation fails generically, giving no clues about account existence or token state. Upon success, the user can immediately login with the new password.

Only the token and password, both validated for format and policy, are processed, with no side-effects elsewhere in the user table. This ensures privacy and secure account recovery, per documented requirements.

Related authentication flows: forgot password (initiation), login, session refresh. Audit logging and token invalidation are system responsibilities, not user facing.
operations.summary: Reset user password in 'todo_users' (given a valid reset token); update hash and 'updated_at'.

requestBody.description: Token and new password to set. Password must meet policy.

responseBody.description: Confirmation that password was reset and account is now accessible with updated login.

operations.name: completePasswordReset

operations.specification: Allow a logged-in user to change their password by proving current login (via session) and providing a new password that meets strength policy. Compares user credentials in 'todo_users' table, updates 'password_hash', timestamps 'updated_at', and ensures that all refresh tokens are revoked (by marking sessions in 'todo_user_sessions' as expired). This endpoint strictly validates existing credentials and prevents continued use of old credentials.
operations.description:
This operation enables an authenticated user to change their own password, enforcing identity via current session and verifying the old password against 'todo_users.password_hash'. The new password is hashed and stored, then the 'updated_at' timestamp is updated. All user sessions (records in 'todo_user_sessions') are invalidated by updating their 'expired_at' field, ensuring that only future logins will succeed with the new credentials.

The endpoint requires the old and new passwords, the former for validation and the latter for updating. Failure returns a generic error, never indicating which credential is wrong. Security policies and audit trail constraints (not shown here) are upheld at all points. No other user data is modified.

This is the correct operation for enforcing password rotation, recovery from compromise, and conformance to password strength rules.

Related endpoints: session refresh (for re-login), password reset for forgotten passwords.
operations.summary: Change current password for the authenticated user in 'todo_users', updating password hash and session expiry.

requestBody.description: Old and new passwords for credential update. Checks old, hashes and stores new (must meet policy).

responseBody.description: Report of password change and confirmation of session revocation for re-authentication.

operations.name: changePassword

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a paginated and filtered list of user accounts. It operates on the todo_users table, supporting advanced filtering, sorting, and pagination to allow each user to query only their own account. Email is unique per the Prisma schema. Only authenticated users can use this operation, and the response type is summary-optimized for list context.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated and filtered list of user accounts in the system.

This operation returns user summary information such as unique identifier and email. Filtering and searching are primarily used internally, as each user can only access their own account due to strict access controls described in the functional requirements and enforced by the underlying Prisma schema. The purpose is to allow queries like self-profile viewing or email existence checks, not global user enumeration.

Security is paramount: only the authenticated user can see their own information—no user can see others' data. The operation enforces this by requiring the session's userId to match the returned entity. Fields in the response conform to the todo_users schema, ensuring consistency and reliability. Invalid or unauthenticated requests will result in authentication or validation errors per error-handling requirements.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve a filtered, paginated list of user accounts (todo_users).

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering user accounts. Used for querying own account or implementing self-service queries.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of user summary information matching search criteria. Only the authenticated user's own account is visible.

operations.name: index

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves the details of a specific user account by its unique ID. It is backed by the todo_users table, leveraging the id field defined as the primary key in the Prisma schema. This read-only operation is used by each user to retrieve their own account details.

Strict ownership validation ensures that the userId provided must correspond to the authenticated user; otherwise, the request is denied. The response contains the detailed user entity information as defined in the todo_users schema, including fields such as id, email, and timestamps.
operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information for a specific user account by ID.

This operation enables a user to fetch their own profile data using their unique userId. Access is strictly limited: authenticated users can only request their own information, and the system rigorously enforces this via ID/user session matching and validation logic.

The returned data structure aligns exactly with the todo_users schema, providing all relevant metadata regarding the user's account and supporting robust client-side profile management. Unauthorized or out-of-scope access attempts are blocked and logged in accordance with system security requirements.
operations.summary: Retrieve detail information for a user account (todo_users) by userId.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target user.

responseBody.description: The complete user entity detail for the specified userId, if and only if owned by the requester.

operations.name: at

operations.specification: This API operation updates an existing user account in the Todo List system. It is associated with the todo_users table, which handles all private user credentials and account metadata for the application. The update process allows modification of user-managed fields, such as email and password, as defined in the Prisma schema, and must respect validation for uniqueness and secure password requirements per schema documentation. Only allowable user attributes (such as email and password_hash) can be changed, and the operation enforces business rules for field updates, leveraging unique and data integrity constraints at the database level.
operations.description:
Update the account information for a specific user in the Todo List application.

This endpoint enables changes to the user's email address or password, provided the correct user identifier is supplied. The operation enforces strong data validation: email addresses must be unique, and password updates require a secure hash format, as outlined in the underlying Prisma schema's field descriptions. Both successful and failed update attempts are accurately timestamped for auditability via the user's updated_at column.

Security is critical: only authenticated users are permitted to update their own account, and all sensitive operations (especially password changes) require re-authentication with the valid current password or a secure session. Implementation must guard against privilege escalation and prevent modification of other users' records.

The request body is validated for syntactic correctness (email format, password strength, and compliance with application constraints). Unknown or extra fields are disregarded. Any update triggers a refresh of the updated_at timestamp and ensures the system’s integrity is maintained throughout the process.
operations.summary: Update a todo user’s account (todo_users table)

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target user account to update.

requestBody.description: Data to update the user account, such as new email or password hash.

responseBody.description: The updated user account information after changes are applied.

operations.name: update

operations.specification: This API operation permanently erases a user account from the todo_users table, removing all credentials and identity records for the minimal Todo List application. Deletion is cascade-compliant: removing a user triggers automatic removal of all dependent data per schema’s referential integrity description. No fields are assumed to exist beyond those defined in the Prisma schema; role management and soft deletion are not present, thus, deletion is immediate and irreversible.
operations.description:
Delete the specified user account from the Todo List application.

When this operation is invoked, the identified user’s record is immediately removed from the database, following cascading delete behavior as described in the prisma schema documentation. This ensures that all sessions, todos, and related user-specific records are also removed for compliance and privacy purposes.

Only an authenticated user may delete their own account. Access controls must prevent users from deleting accounts that do not belong to them. The operation is designed to preserve system integrity and guarantee that no residual personal data remains after a user-initiated account removal.
operations.summary: Delete a todo user account (todo_users table)

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the user account to delete.

responseBody.description: Deleted user account information or null upon success.

operations.name: erase

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves all authentication sessions that belong to a specific user in the minimal Todo application. It operates on the todo_user_sessions table, which records each user login session entry along with context such as IP, href, referrer, timestamps, and session state. Designed primarily for audit and security review, this endpoint enables filtered and paginated lookup of all sessions for a user without exposing or allowing modification of any authentication state directly via this API.

The endpoint requires the unique identifier (UUID) of the target user as a path parameter, ensuring only session records belonging to that user are returned. The operation supports structured queries, pagination, and sorting, intended for review such as security audits, suspicious login investigation, or manual session review.

This API is strictly read-only and excluded from any session creation, update, or deletion; it is safe for security monitoring but NOT for user authentication lifecycle management. All sensitive fields (e.g., IP) are included for audit purposes. Sessions for all states (active, revoked, expired, etc.) are returned.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated, filterable list of authentication sessions associated with the specified user in the Todo List application.

This operation provides support for investigating account activity, tracking abnormal login patterns, or reviewing system security posture. The response includes session metadata such as login IP, HTTP referrer, and session initiation URL, which enables complete traceability per privacy and audit requirements. The API provides robust query capabilities, allowing session lookups based on time created, expiration status, or other attributes.

All data returned is sourced directly from the todo_user_sessions table, whose schema includes strong guarantees on audit trace completeness. Attempts to access this endpoint rely on business-specific design; generic read-only session data is not privileged. No session manipulation (creation, update, revocation) is supported. Similar endpoints include GET /users/{userId}/sessions/{sessionId} for per-session detail, but this is the list/index operation for review across multiple sessions.
operations.summary: List and search all sessions for a given user (todo_user_sessions table, public view).

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target user whose sessions will be listed

requestBody.description: Session search filters and pagination configuration for the index operation. Queries may specify time range, status, and sort options.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of user session summaries matching search criteria, for audit and review.

operations.name: index

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves the full detail for a specific authentication session record tied to a given todo user account. Operating on the todo_user_sessions table, it provides all metadata about a login session: IP, href, referrer, creation/expiration timestamps, state, and linkage to the owning user. This API endpoint requires both the user ID and the session ID (each UUIDs) to uniquely identify and authorize access to the session.

Primary use case is for audit and system investigation to correlate user activity to session data and satisfy privacy-compliant requirements. All fields in the todo_user_sessions table are returned in full, with no data omitted or masked. Only valid session records associated with the specified user ID may be accessed; attempts to query for nonexistent or unrelated session IDs are denied.

Operation is strictly read-only as mandated by minimal requirements. No modifications to session state or data are permitted. This endpoint complements the index/search endpoint, completing the review tooling for user session management.
operations.description:
Fetch the complete metadata and audit information for an individual authentication session for a given user in the Todo application.

This endpoint is for audit or review purposes and displays all data stored in the todo_user_sessions table for the specific login session identified by both userId and sessionId. Returned data includes origin IP address, referer URL, session creation and expiration information, all as required for system compliance.

System returns data traceable to the owning user (todo_users). If the specified session does not exist or is not linked to the given user, a not-found or permission-denied error is triggered. This API never exposes session tokens/credentials and does not allow session deletion or updates. For bulk session review, PATCH /users/{userId}/sessions should be used.
operations.summary: View full details of a specific session for a user (todo_user_sessions table, public view).

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the user owning the session

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: Unique session record identifier (UUID) within the todo_user_sessions table

responseBody.description: All fields from the todo_user_sessions record for the selected session, including IP and audit metadata.

operations.name: at

operations.specification: This operation queries the todo_todos table to retrieve a paginated, filtered list of todos owned by the authenticated user. The endpoint allows searching, filtering by completion status, date range, and ordering by creation or last update timestamps. It enforces strict filtering so that only the requesting user's own todos are returned, supporting privacy and multi-device consistency. All input fields, filtering rules, and search parameters strictly follow business requirements and validation rules documented in both the requirements analysis and Prisma schema.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated, filtered, and sorted list of the authenticated user's todo items from the system.

The operation provides full-text and partial description matching, filtering by completion status (incomplete or complete), and date range search on creation or update timestamps. Pagination is required to support scalability and performance, with configurable page size and cursor/offset options. Sorting can be applied based on creation or update date, with default sort being most recently updated first.

Security: Only authenticated users can access this endpoint. All queries are automatically scoped to the user's own data using the authenticated user context from the JWT/session. Users will never see data owned by others, and attempts to access other users' data will be denied. Validation on filter/sort input prevents malformed queries or overloading the service.

Related endpoints include GET /todos/{todoId} for fetching individual items, and all modification/deletion actions are run via separate endpoints. Batch operations are not allowed through this endpoint.

All search and filtering criteria are enforced as per requirements/business rules. If no todos match the criteria or the user has no todos, an empty result set is returned with appropriate pagination metadata.
operations.summary: Search, filter, and paginate the authenticated user's todos (todo_todos table).

requestBody.description: Pagination, filtering, and search parameters for listing user's todos.

responseBody.description: Paginated result set of todos owned by the authenticated user matching filtering/search criteria.

operations.name: index

operations.specification: This operation retrieves detailed information for a specific todo from the todo_todos table based on its unique identifier. Ownership is strictly enforced—only the authenticated owner can retrieve details for their todo item, and attempts to access another user's item will be denied. All business validation and access control are strictly referenced from requirements and schema comments to ensure privacy and compliance.
operations.description:
Retrieve the full detail of a specific todo item, but ONLY if it is owned by the authenticated user.

This endpoint enforces strict ownership isolation: the system will not disclose the existence or details of todos owned by other users. When invoked with a valid todoId, the operation fetches the item if and only if ownership matches the authenticated user. Unauthorized access attempts are not only denied but are indistinguishable from "not found" for privacy.

Validation includes ensuring the todoId is a valid UUID and refers to an existing, active todo. Security is provided by scoping every lookup to the user's own data based on the authenticated JWT/session. No other fields or users' todos can be fetched or inferred using this endpoint.

This endpoint serves as the foundation for detail views in user interfaces and for initiating updates, deletions, or status changes. Errors for missing or unauthorized access are always handled using generic messages as per privacy guidelines.
operations.summary: Retrieve details of a specific todo item owned by the authenticated user (todo_todos table).

parameters.name: todoId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target todo item.

responseBody.description: Full details of the user's own todo item, if found and owned.

operations.name: at

prerequisites.description: A todo item must be created by the authenticated user before it can be retrieved. This establishes the existence of the todo referenced by todoId.

operations.specification: This operation creates a new todo item for the authenticated user. It operates on the todo_todos table, ensuring that each todo is exclusively owned and managed by a single user. On creation, the todo item requires a non-empty description between 1 and 255 characters, is initially set to incomplete, and timestamps for creation and last update are set. The user_id foreign key is automatically set to the requesting user, enforcing strict privacy and data isolation. All constraints, input trimming, and business rules are enforced according to the loaded Prisma schema and requirements files.
operations.description:
Create a new todo item for the authenticated user.

This endpoint allows authenticated users to create a new todo task by providing a valid description field. Only a description is accepted for creation; all other fields such as ownership, creation timestamps, and completion status are managed by the system.

Business requirements and validation are strictly enforced: the description must be non-empty after trimming and no longer than 255 characters. The new todo is always associated with the requesting user, using their identity extracted from the authentication context. The initial completion status is set to false and a created_at/updated_at timestamp is recorded.

No user may create todos for any other user. If the user has already reached the maximum active todo limit (typically 1,000), the system will reject creation with a clear error message. Upon success, the full details of the created todo are returned. Security, ownership, and privacy rules are strictly enforced as described in the official requirements and schema definitions.
operations.summary: Create a new todo item (todo_todos table) for the authenticated user.

requestBody.description: Fields for creating a new todo item: only the description is required and accepted from the client.

responseBody.description: The detailed todo item record created for the user.

operations.name: create

operations.specification: This operation updates an existing todo item owned by the authenticated user. It modifies the todo_todos table entry with the provided todoId, verifying that the todo exists and is owned by the requesting user. Only the description (1-255 trimmed chars) and completion (is_completed) status are updatable; all other fields are managed by the system. Ownership, privacy, and timestamp update logic is enforced as per the Prisma schema and requirements. The update operation will refuse to modify records that don't exist, are owned by other users, or violate business/length constraints.
operations.description:
Update an existing todo item owned by the authenticated user.

This endpoint enables authenticated users to edit the description and completion state of a specific todo, which must be owned by them. The todoId in the path must refer to an existing todo belonging to the user, and the request body may include a new description and/or change the completion status.

Strict validation occurs for the description (if provided): it must be non-empty and below the maximum character limit after trimming whitespace. When is_completed is toggled, the completion timestamp is appropriately set or cleared, and updated_at is always set. Attempting to update a todo owned by anyone else, or non-existent, will result in a permission or not found error, protecting data privacy. All other fields are managed by the backend and are not updatable via this endpoint.

This operation implements all business, validation, and audit rules outlined in the requirements and schema comments.
operations.summary: Update a todo (description and/or completion status) in the todo_todos table.

parameters.name: todoId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target todo item to update.

requestBody.description: Fields to update for the todo: description (validated, optional), is_completed (optional).

responseBody.description: The updated todo item details after changes are applied.

operations.name: update

prerequisites.description: A todo item must be created before it can be updated; ensures todoId in the path refers to an existing record belonging to the authenticated user.

operations.specification: This operation permanently deletes a single todo item from the todo_todos Prisma table. The operation is designed to enforce strict ownership and privacy: only the authenticated user who owns the todo may perform the deletion. The todo is uniquely identified by its id (UUID), and all business validation and access control are enforced in accordance with the schema definition. Deletion is permanent and irreversible, fully removing the item and its associated metadata from persistent storage. The operation scopes the delete to a single user's todo history and is not accessible to other users or administrative roles, ensuring user privacy and individual task management integrity.
operations.description:
Permanently remove a todo item owned by the authenticated user from the system database.

This operation is accessible only to authenticated users, and strictly enforces that each user may delete only their own todos. The todo item is identified by its unique UUID in the path parameter. Upon successful execution, the referenced todo and all its metadata (description, completion status, timestamps) are erased, and the operation is irreversible—deleted items cannot be restored.

Security is critical: The user_id foreign key link ensures only the item's owner can execute this operation; attempts by other users or unauthorized actors will result in permission denied errors. No soft deletion is implemented; the delete is permanent as defined by the schema's lack of a soft-delete column or strategy. This matches the privacy and integrity requirements of the todo_todos model as documented in the database description comments.
operations.summary: Permanently delete a todo item from the todo_todos table.

parameters.name: todoId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target todo item (UUID format). Only the owner may delete their own todos.

operations.name: erase

prerequisites.description: A todo item must be created before it can be deleted; ensures todoId refers to an existing record owned by the requesting user.

authorizations.name: user
authorizations.description: A registered and authenticated user who can create, view, update, and delete their own todo items. Each user manages their own list of todos and cannot access other users' data.

limit.description: Limitation of records per a page.

pages.description:
Total pages.

Equal to {@link records} / {@link limit} with ceiling.

access.description:
JWT access token for authenticated requests.

This token should be included in the Authorization header for subsequent
authenticated API requests as `Bearer {token}`.

refresh.description:
Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

This token can be used to request new access tokens when the current access
token expires, extending the user's session.

expired_at.description:
Access token expiration timestamp.

ISO 8601 date-time string indicating when the access token will expire and
can no longer be used for authentication.

refreshable_until.description:
Refresh token expiration timestamp.

ISO 8601 date-time string indicating the latest time until which the
refresh token can be used to obtain new access tokens.

IAuthorizationToken.description:
Authorization token response structure.

This interface defines the structure of the authorization token response
returned after successful user authentication. It contains both access and
refresh tokens along with their expiration information.

This token structure is automatically included in API schemas when the system
detects authorization actors in the requirements analysis phase. It provides
a standard format for JWT-based authentication across the generated backend
applications.

email.description: User's unique email address for authentication and identity recovery. Must be unique across all user accounts in the system. Validated during registration and used as the primary login credential. Required for account creation and authentication.

password.description: Password entered by the user at registration. Must be at least 8 characters long, containing both letters and numbers to comply with the password policy. The password is hashed on the backend and only the hash is stored in the database. Never stored or transmitted in plain text after authentication.

oneOf.description: IP address at the time of registration (IPv4 address format). Used for session creation and auditing.
IP address at the time of registration (IPv6 address format). Used for session creation and auditing.
IP address is optional and may be omitted. When omitted, the backend will attempt to extract the client IP automatically.

ip.description: Client's IP address when the session is initiated. This field can be null or omitted; the server will extract it if not provided. Used for session creation, context, and audit logging.

href.description: Full URL at the time the join request was submitted (the browser location). Required for proper audit trails and tracing the session's origin.

referrer.description: Referrer URL during the registration request. Required for session context and anti-abuse detection.

ITodoUser.IJoin.description:
DTO for user registration in the minimal Todo List application.

Used in the join operation (`/auth/user/join`). Accepts new user's email and plain-text password (which must comply with the strength policy). Expects proper session context for audit (href and referrer required, IP is optional). This DTO ensures all registration data meets system security and integrity requirements.

Fields are strictly validated. Never includes system-managed or actor-identity fields. The password field is mapped to the `password_hash` column in Prisma after secure hashing. Email uniqueness is enforced in the database.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the authenticated user account, auto-generated at registration.

This identifier maps directly to the 'id' column (UUID) in the 'todo_users' database table. It is used throughout the system for reference and cross-entity relationships. This value never changes during the account's lifetime.

email.description:
The user's unique email associated with their account at registration.

Email is the principal identity and authentication credential and is never exposed or returned except directly to the authenticated subject. Used for audit context and system activity logs.

created_at.description:
Timestamp for when the user account was originally created in the system.

This field is set only once, at registration time, and remains immutable throughout the account lifecycle. It supports audit requirements for traceability and compliance on user onboarding timing.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp for the most recent update to this user's account, including email, password, or critical metadata changes.

Field is automatically updated by the backend whenever the user's record changes. Used for historical analysis, security investigations, and detailed audit history.

ITodoUser.IAuthorized.description:
Authentication payload returned after successful user registration or login.

This schema provides, in a minimal, privacy-respecting form, only those user and session details required for future authenticated requests. It includes the user's unguessable identifier, the email for audit purposes, system timestamps for onboarding/change detection, and authentication tokens for request authorization.

Strict privacy, compliance, and security requirements are enforced. No sensitive information from the user record beyond identity and token details is exposed. The schema aligns with system policy and privacy guarantees throughout the application's operations.

email.description:
User's unique email address used for authentication and identity recovery. Must match a unique record in 'todo_users'.

This value serves as the principal login credential and is checked at login using the system's unique index constraint. Ensures strict separation between users and sensitivity to account privacy. Required field for all authentication operations.

password.description:
Plain text user password submitted for authentication. Must be a minimum of 8 and a maximum of 128 characters, as enforced by security policy.

Password is never persisted in clear text. Used only transiently for cryptographic validation against password_hash in the user record. Required for every credential-based authentication transaction.

oneOf.description: Client's IP address during login for audit, security, and session traceability. Collected in session context, stored via 'ip' in 'todo_user_sessions'. May be omitted and set automatically by backend if not provided, but the client should supply when available.

ip.description:
Client's IP address during login, or null if not provided.

This information is critical for comprehensive audit logs, anomaly detection, and detailed session traceability. Backend services will attempt to set this automatically when missing, but providing it in the request enhances security and monitoring controls.

href.description:
URL of the page from which authentication is initiated (the current browser location at login).

This information ensures each session creation or login event is accompanied by provenance information, which supports legal compliance, audit trails, and security investigation requirements. It is stored in the session audit record.

referrer.description:
HTTP referrer URL when login is initiated. Used for advanced session meta tracking in 'todo_user_sessions'.

This value provides context for where the login originated (such as previous website). Required in all authentication events to fulfill audit, compliance, and anti-abuse requirements.

ITodoUser.ILogin.description:
User login credentials required for authentication.

This DTO is used by the login endpoint and collects minimal credential data (email and password), as well as comprehensive session and origin context (ip, href, referrer).

Upon authentication, this data is written to audit logs and session records, supporting incident analysis, privacy investigations, and system auditing. All fields are strictly validated and processed following privacy, security, and compliance policies.

refresh_token.description: The refresh token issued at initial login or from previous refresh. Used to authorize renewal of authentication and is validated against active session entries in 'todo_user_sessions'. Must be at least 16 characters and match one of the registered/valid records. Never exposes internal structure or raw storage format.

oneOf.description: Client's IP address for token refresh. Used for session auditing and stored via 'ip' in 'todo_user_sessions'. May be omitted/null, but should be provided by client if available.

ip.description: Client's IP address for this token refresh session, or null if not available.

href.description: URL of the page when the refresh operation is initiated. Used for audit context in new session record in 'todo_user_sessions'. Required every time a refresh is performed.

referrer.description: HTTP referrer URL for the refresh session. Used as audit context in new 'todo_user_sessions' entry. Required for compliance and traceability.

ITodoUser.IRefresh.description: DTO for user authentication token refresh. Contains the refresh token plus connection context fields required for session tracking in 'todo_user_sessions'. Session context fields (href, referrer, ip) are necessary for security auditing and advanced privacy compliance. These attributes are recorded each time the refresh is performed.

email.description: Registered email address for password reset. Must be a valid email and match the 'email' field in the 'todo_users' table. The system never indicates whether this email exists. Used solely to initiate a secure password reset flow.

ITodoUser.IResetPasswordRequest.description:
Payload to initiate the password reset process for users unable to sign in. Contains only an email field, which must match the existing user records. If the email exists, a password reset token will be sent; otherwise, a generic response is returned to prevent account enumeration. No state change occurs at this stage. Rate-limiting and auditing are handled elsewhere.

Used when a user cannot access their account and needs to trigger password reset (out-of-band recovery).

success.description: Indicates whether the reset flow was successfully initiated (request accepted for processing). Response is always generic to prevent leaking account existence or system policy details. True only signals request acceptance, not the email’s validity or delivery status.

ITodoUser.IResetPasswordResponse.description: Response for password reset initiation. Always generic: never reveals whether an email address exists or a token was sent. Used to prevent information leaks and enumerate existing users. Indicates only that the request was received and the reset flow (if applicable) is underway. Actual token delivery is handled out-of-band, and real errors are handled internally (rate-limiting, audit logging, etc.).

ITodoUser.IResetPasswordComplete.description:
Input schema for completing a password reset in the Todo List system.

Represents the payload submitted along with a password-reset token. Captures the one-time-use token and the new password for updating the user's credentials in the 'todo_users' table. Designed for maximum security, this DTO collects only essential fields; user identity is inferred entirely from the password reset token (never submitted as email or userId).

Password field is validated for strength and policy on the backend. The password is provided as plain text for secure hashing. No authentication, session, or identifying fields are present in this schema (token is opaque; password is confidential). Only password hash will be changed in user record, no other updates.

Single-use and time-limited policy for tokens is strictly enforced; audit logs updated per business compliance requirements.

token.description:
An opaque, single-use, and time-limited password reset token previously issued to the user's registered email.

Used to securely associate this reset operation with the correct user account. Value is typically a cryptographically random string (not guessable or derivable), but may use URL-safe characters. Never reused. Only backend can resolve its meaning.

Invalid, missing, expired, or previously used tokens are rejected without exposing user existence or state.

password.description:
New plain-text password chosen by the user.

Must meet system password complexity policy (minimum 8 characters, recommended to include uppercase, lowercase, number, and symbol for enhanced security; absolute max 72 characters for full bcrypt/argon2 compatibility). Will be securely hashed and stored in 'password_hash' column in 'todo_users'.

Plain password is never stored or logged. Backend is responsible for hashing. This is the only field used to update user credentials.

ITodoUser.IResetPasswordResult.description:
Response schema indicating the result of a successful password reset via token completion for a Todo List user.

Returned after a password reset operation has validated the provided token, accepted a new password, and updated 'password_hash' field for the identified 'todo_users' account. Serves only as confirmation that credentials have been reset and user may now login with the new password.

Contains only a message for client display; does not disclose which user was affected. No sensitive or identifying information is ever returned.

message.description: Confirmation message that the user's password has been successfully reset. Describes that credentials have been updated and the user may now log in using the new password.

ITodoUser.IChangePassword.description:
DTO for changing a user's password in the minimal Todo application.

This schema represents the payload required for a logged-in user to change their password. The user must provide their current password for verification and a new password that meets the application's password strength requirements.

On successful submission, the old password will be checked against the bcrypt hash in 'todo_users.password_hash', and if valid, 'password_hash' will be updated with the hash of 'newPassword' and 'updated_at' timestamp is modified. All outstanding sessions will be invalidated for security compliance.

This DTO is used only for authenticated actions and must never accept user or session IDs from client input. All context regarding the authenticated user is established server-side.

oldPassword.description: The user's current password in plain text. Used for credential verification against the stored 'password_hash'. Must be provided by the user attempting to change their password. Not stored, used only for verification during this operation.

newPassword.description: The new password the user wishes to set. Must meet all password policy rules enforced by the application (minimum 8 characters, at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one number, and one special character recommended). Will be securely hashed server-side and stored in 'password_hash'. Not stored in plain text.

ITodoUser.IChangePasswordResult.description:
Result response for a successful password change operation on the authenticated user.

Indicates the user's password was updated, all user sessions were invalidated (logout required), and the user must re-authenticate with their new password. If requested, may include audit or trace data, but no sensitive credentials are ever returned.

This DTO is the response to changing password and confirms the effect of session revocation for all current and future logins.

success.description: Indicates whether the password change was executed successfully. True if credentials were updated and sessions invalidated.

message.description: Human-readable message confirming password change and session expiry. Used for client display, not for logic.

ITodoUser.IRequest.description:
Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering user accounts in the Todo List application.

This type is used for paginated queries targeting the user's own account, usually for self-profile lookup or existence checks, not for global enumeration of users. Filtering and sorting are internally validated, as only the authenticated user can view their own information. All fields correspond to columns and query capabilities defined in the todo_users Prisma schema, including unique email. Only the authenticated user can perform this search, and results conform to privacy and security policies.

page.description: Pagination parameter: The current page number for the search result set. Must be a positive integer. Used internally as only single-user paging is allowed.

limit.description: Limiting parameter: The maximum number of user summary records to return in a page. Must be between 1 and 50. Used primarily to restrict payloads and ensure single-user privacy.

search.description: Optional search term for user accounts. Typically matches email substring. Only usable for self-profile lookup, not to enumerate all users.

oneOf.description: Sorting criteria for user list. Can be 'email', 'created_at', or 'updated_at'—all indexed columns in todo_users Prisma model. Default and allowed values match business requirements.
Sorting criteria for user list. Can be 'email', 'created_at', or 'updated_at'—all indexed columns in todo_users Prisma model. Default and allowed values match business requirements.
Sorting criteria for user list. Can be 'email', 'created_at', or 'updated_at'—all indexed columns in todo_users Prisma model. Default and allowed values match business requirements.

order_by.description: Sorting criteria for user list. Can be 'email', 'created_at', or 'updated_at'—all indexed columns in todo_users Prisma model. Default and allowed values match business requirements.

oneOf.description: Sorting direction. Either ascending ('asc') or descending ('desc'). Sanity-checked server-side as user can only see their own data.
Sorting direction. Either ascending ('asc') or descending ('desc'). Sanity-checked server-side as user can only see their own data.

order_direction.description: Sorting direction. Either ascending ('asc') or descending ('desc'). Sanity-checked server-side as user can only see their own data.

ITodoUser.description:
Entity type for a user account record in the Todo List application.

Models a private user and their authentication metadata, as represented in the todo_users table. Includes unique email, securely hashed password, and auto-generated timestamps for account creation and updates. Security and privacy are integral—no password or actor fields are ever exposed in response types. All business logic, field requirements, and uniqueness constraints correspond to the Prisma schema and requirements documentation for strict privacy, integrity, and user isolation.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user account. Matches the primary key (id) in the todo_users schema and used for all authentication, authorization, and ownership checks.

email.description: User's unique email address for authentication and recovery. Must be unique in the system, validated at creation, and respected as privacy boundary.

created_at.description: Timestamp recording when the user account was created. Auto-generated and immutable.

updated_at.description: Timestamp for the most recent update to this user's account, including email or password changes. Updated automatically.

id.description: Primary key for the user. Unique, unguessable identifier for user account records. Sourced from `todo_users.id` in Prisma schema.

email.description: User's unique email address for authentication and identity recovery. Must be unique in the system per privacy and login requirements. Sourced from `todo_users.email` in Prisma schema.

created_at.description: Timestamp for when the user account was created. Used for audit and ordering. Sourced from `todo_users.created_at` in Prisma schema.

updated_at.description: Timestamp for the most recent update to this user's account (email, password, etc). Sourced from `todo_users.updated_at` in Prisma schema.

ITodoUser.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary of a todo_users account entity.

Provides essential account and audit information for display in lists, references, or API responses where the full user record is not required. Excludes any authentication, password hash, or sensitive fields by design to minimize risk and surface only non-sensitive identity and metadata. All fields must exist in the underlying todo_users table.

email.description: User's unique email address for authentication and identity recovery. Must be unique in the system per privacy and login requirements.

password.description: The user's password in plain text (for update/change actions). Clients submit the new desired password in this field—backend will hash and store securely. This field must be strong, with a minimum length as required by security best practices. Will never be returned in any response. Cannot update directly to password_hash.

ITodoUser.IUpdate.description:
DTO for updating user-managed fields of the Todo User account such as email or password. All changes are validated for uniqueness, security, and auditability per the business requirements and Prisma table comment.

Sensitive or system-managed fields (id, password_hash, timestamps) MUST NOT be accepted in this DTO. Only user-editable information may be supplied. Changing the password triggers backend hashing logic and appropriate update to password_hash in storage.

page.description: Pagination parameter: the page number to retrieve. Defaults to 1 if not specified.

limit.description: Pagination parameter: number of records per page. Defaults to a sensible value (such as 20) with a maximum of 100.

created_from.description: Filter: Only sessions created at or after this ISO 8601 timestamp will be included in the result.

created_to.description: Filter: Only sessions created before this ISO 8601 timestamp (exclusive) will be included in the result.

expired.description: Filter: Set true to retrieve only expired sessions, or false for only active ones. If omitted, both are included.

ITodoUserSession.IRequest.description: DTO for paginated, filterable retrieval of Todo User session records for audit and security review. Provides pagination controls and common filters relevant for session history review—in line with the todo_user_sessions Prisma table. Does not allow session creation or manipulation.

id.description: Primary key for the session. Unique identifier for each authentication session instance.

todo_user_id.description: Foreign key referencing the owner of this session. Links each session to a specific user. {@link todo_users.id}.

ip.description: IP address from which the session was initiated for auditing and session traceability.

href.description: URL at the time session was created, for security audit and origin verification.

referrer.description: HTTP referrer when session was created, for basic session tracing and anti-abuse context.

created_at.description: Timestamp for when the session was established.

expired_at.description: Timestamp for when the session expired, was revoked, or logged out. Null if session is active.

ITodoUserSession.description:
Authentication session record for a user in the Todo List application.

Contains all metadata capturing details of a user's login session including audit trail and connection context. Tied to a specific user, this schema covers session lifecycle (creation and expiration), source IP, and referer data for complete traceability.

Provided for audit, compliance, and investigation use cases. All fields match the todo_user_sessions database table as per privacy and security requirements.

page.description: Page number for pagination. Must be a positive integer. Determines which page of results is returned.

limit.description: Maximum number of todos returned per page. Must be a positive integer within allowed system limits.

search.description: Full-text or partial search query matching description field of todos.

is_completed.description: If true, filter for completed todos; if false, filter for only incomplete items. If omitted, all todos are returned regardless of completion.

created_from.description: Filters todos created at or after this timestamp. ISO 8601 format.

created_to.description: Filters todos created at or before this timestamp. ISO 8601 format.

updated_from.description: Filters todos updated at or after this timestamp. ISO 8601 format.

updated_to.description: Filters todos updated at or before this timestamp. ISO 8601 format.

oneOf.description: Selects the field used for sorting results. Must be one of 'created_at' or 'updated_at'.
Selects the field used for sorting results. Must be one of 'created_at' or 'updated_at'.

order_by.description: Selects the field used for sorting results. Must be one of 'created_at' or 'updated_at'.

order_desc.description: If true, sort results in descending order; if false, ascending order.

ITodoTodo.IRequest.description:
Filtering, pagination, and search parameters for user todo list API.

Allows the client to specify paging, text search, completion filtering, date ranges, and sorting for listing the authenticated user's todos. All queries are always scoped to the current user via authentication context, never by user_id parameter. System enforces validation and safe defaults if omitted. All fields map to filtering capabilities documented by business rules.

id.description: Primary key for the todo item. Universally unique identifier ensuring each todo is distinct within the system.

description.description: User-supplied description of the todo item. Must be between 1 and 255 characters after whitespace trimming. Required for creation and all updates, as per business requirement for meaningful task details.

is_completed.description: Completion status indicating whether the todo is finished (true) or incomplete (false). Set to false on creation and only toggled by owner.

oneOf.description: Timestamp marking when the todo was last marked as complete. Null if never completed or if reset when marked incomplete.
Null if the todo is either never completed or was reset to incomplete.

completed_at.description: Represents the completion datetime, or null if not completed. Used for audit trails and user progress tracking.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the todo item was first created. Immutable. Used for audit and ordering.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this todo (including description edits or completion state change).

user.description: Reference to the owning user (privacy enforced: only available to the owner). Transformed from user_id foreign key, includes only summary information for UI.

ITodoTodo.description:
Full detail representation of a single todo item. Represents a user's personal task in the todo list, with strict ownership and privacy enforced at the system level.

Includes status, audit information, and references to the owning user. Only the owner may access, modify, or view this entity. Business logic as per requirements and Prisma schema guarantees that all required fields are present, inputs are validated, and ownership is not mutable via API.

description.description: User-supplied description for the new todo item. Must be non-empty after trimming (1-255 characters). Only client-provided property; all others are managed by the server.

ITodoTodo.ICreate.description: Create request for a new todo item. Accepts only a non-empty description (trimmed, 1-255 chars) as input. All ownership and state are assigned by the backend using the authentication context (user id), with completion status and timestamps automatically managed. Enforces security and business rules outlined in requirements and Prisma schema.

description.description: User-supplied description of the todo item. Must be between 1 and 255 characters after whitespace is trimmed. Editable during update; required for business logic enforcement. Sourced from `todo_todos.description` in Prisma schema.

is_completed.description: Completion status of this todo. If provided, updates the completion state. True if complete, false if incomplete. Sourced from `todo_todos.is_completed` in Prisma schema.

ITodoTodo.IUpdate.description:
Update request body for a todo item in the todo_todos table.

Enables partial modification of the description or completed state for an individually owned todo. Only the content and completion status are updatable; all identification, ownership, and timestamps are system-controlled. Each update is validated for ownership, field constraints, and business rules as enforced by the backend.

Fields:
- description: Optional. If provided, must satisfy length and non-blank constraints after trimming.
- is_completed: Optional. If provided, updates completion status and related timestamps. All unauthorized, unauthorized, or invalid actions are blocked at the business logic layer.

ITodoUserSession.ISummary.description:
Summary type for a user authentication session in the minimal Todo List application.

Represents essential audit and traceability fields for a single session, omitting sensitive/internal details. Used in list responses and embedding in user/session-related contexts.
Includes key session linkage, connection metadata, and lifecycle timestamps, mapped directly from the todo_user_sessions model.

This type is safe for public display as part of a user’s session history or security log, and can be referenced in todo user detail views as an embedded summary.

id.description: Unique identifier of the authentication session. Directly maps to todo_user_sessions.id and serves as the session’s primary key.

todo_user_id.description: ID of the owning user for the session. Reference to todo_users.id. Used for audit and context linking; do not expose user personal information in session summaries.

ip.description: IP address from which the session was initiated. Used for traceability and anomaly detection; directly from the ip column.

href.description: Originating page URL at login/session start. Useful for audit trail and context-aware security features.

referrer.description: Referrer URL recorded when the session was established. Supports anti-abuse analytics and origin chain validation.

created_at.description: Timestamp when session was created. Used for security audit and session lifecycle analysis.

oneOf.description: Timestamp when this session was marked as expired, revoked, or logged out. Null if session is still active.

expired_at.description: Nullable session expiration timestamp. Set if session is expired or logged out; null if session is currently active.

ITodoTodo.ISummary.description:
Summary type for a personal todo item in the minimal Todo List application.

Captures the essential attributes of a todo task for list and embedding purposes, focusing on identifiers, core business fields, and audit lifecycle timestamps. Omits large text fields or deep relations for list efficiency.

Used in todo list views, summaries on user profiles, or any compact representation of a todo’s state and history. Properties directly map from the todo_todos Prisma model, strictly following DB field constraints.

id.description: Unique identifier for the todo item. Primary key for the todo_todos table.

user_id.description: Foreign key referencing the owning user. Privacy-critical property (maps to todo_users.id) but safe in summaries due to lack of personal information; do not expose user details directly here.

description.description: Short description of the todo item. Must be between 1 and 255 UTF-8 characters. Required for creation and every update; corresponds to the description column.

is_completed.description: Flag marking whether the todo is complete. True for completed tasks, false for pending. Directly from is_completed in DB.

oneOf.description: Timestamp when the todo was last marked as complete.

completed_at.description: Nullable timestamp for last completion event. Null if never completed or after being marked incomplete.

created_at.description: Time when the todo item was created in the system. Corresponds to creation lifecycle event.

updated_at.description: Time of the last modification to this todo. Corresponds to update lifecycle event.
